chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a killed person is found and only flesh is found without bones for him, he is not prayed upon; and if bones are found without flesh, he is prayed upon.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on funeral prayer if only bones or only flesh of the deceased are found?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the juristic principle that the presence of a 'core' structural element (bone) preserves the identity of the deceased for ritual purposes, whereas mere flesh is considered insufficient. This distinction is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of Salat al-Janazah when the body is not fully intact, reflecting a pragmatic approach to death rituals amidst varying degrees of decomposition. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the physical continuity of the body as a vessel for the soul's honor, even in partial states.
